label: private_key
description: A whole BEGIN/END private-key block, body included. Non-greedy and (?s)/DOTALL so the body is consumed WHOLE rather than piecemeal — which is also why it is listed first. Known NOT to catch: a key pasted without its armour lines.
sample:
-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----
MIIEowIBAAKCAQEA0000000000000000000000
not a real key, just the shape
-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----

label: bearer_token
description: An Authorization header's value. Anchored with a LOOKBEHIND so the header name survives the redaction and the audit trail stays readable. Known NOT to catch: a token on a line that never names the header (that is what the shape-specific rules are for).

label: api_key
description: A provider-shaped API key: an sk-/sk-ant-/pk- prefix plus a long opaque tail. This is the rule that catches a PRIVATE-PROXY key, which is nobody's published format and which no vendor corpus can know about. Known NOT to catch: a key with no recognisable prefix at all.

label: aws_access_key_id
description: An AWS access key id. Known NOT to catch: the paired SECRET access key, which is a bare 40-character base64 blob with no prefix to anchor on — use a `secret_assignment`-style rule for that.

label: github_token
description: A GitHub personal-access / OAuth / user / server / refresh token. Deliberately open-ended at {16,} rather than pinned to today's length, so a future GitHub token length is still caught. Known NOT to catch: a classic 40-hex GitHub token, which is indistinguishable from a git SHA-1.

label: google_api_key
description: A Google API key. Terminated by \b rather than by a fixed set of delimiters, so it still fires on AIza<35> followed by a bracket or a backslash. Known NOT to catch: a Google OAuth client secret, which carries no AIza prefix.

label: secret_assignment
description: An explicit `password = "..."` / `api_key: '...'` binding. THE reason `replace_group` exists: only the named group `value` is replaced, so `password = ` and its quoting survive and a reviewer can still see WHAT was set without seeing it. Known NOT to catch: a value under six characters, or one containing a space, quote, comma or semicolon.

label: corp-internal-token
description: THE ILLUSTRATIVE ONE — everything above this entry is a built-in expressed in this schema (pointing CD_REDACTIONS at this file verbatim therefore changes nothing about the first seven shapes); this is the kind of rule you actually add. An internal service token. Known NOT to catch: a `corp_` prefixed variable name (too short).
